stories.title: Antimicrobial activity of apramycin formulated with dextran-based single-chain polymeric nanoparticles against Acinetobacter baumannii
stories.description: The global emergence of antimicrobial resistance is driving the development of novel strategies for treating bacterial infections. In this context, dextran-based single-chain polymeric nanoparticles (DXT-SCPNs) have been developed as antibiotic delivery systems for the treatment of pulmonary infections. A series of DXT-SCPNs were formulated with apramycin with different physicochemical properties, namely three degrees of substitution (with a low degree of crosslinking in all cases): low (L-DSa), medium (M-DSa), or high (H-DSa), and two degrees of crosslinking (with a medium degree of substitution in both nanoparticles): low (M-DSa) or high (H-CLa). Their in vitro activity against eleven Acinetobacter baumannii clinical isolates was assessed compared to the free drug, using minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) and time-kill kinetic (TKK) assays. Overall, no statistically significant differences were observed between the antimicrobial activity of free and formulated apramycin. Nevertheless, a slight trend towards higher activity was observed in the cases of M-DSa and H-CLa.
